content:
I am currently working on improving the notations for lambda calculus within CSlib.

Inspired by this blog post and documentation on Lean metaprogramming (unexpanders and parenthesizers), I have successfully implemented basic notations for locally nameless lambda terms using De Bruijn indices.

#check ⟪ (λ λ 2) 3 5 ⟫ₗ
#check (fun (n : Nat) (x : String) (y : Cslib.LambdaCalculus.LocallyNameless.Untyped.Term _) ↦
  ⟪ 3 (λ 5) [y] [fvar "abc"] [fvar x] [bvar n] ⟫ₗ)

My first question is whether there is a conventional way to represent the [_] notation for metavariables. In Lean's notation for syntax, $y is used for antiquotation. I am wondering if using $y instead of [y] would be more intuitive or idiomatic.

I also wanted to improve further more notations like ⟪[bvar n]⟫ₗ and ⟪[fvar "abc"]⟫ₗ. To eliminate the need for explicit bvar and fvar constructors, I defined two coercions to Term Var:

instance {Var : Type} : Coe Nat (Cslib.LambdaCalculus.LocallyNameless.Untyped.Term Var) := ⟨bvar⟩
instance {Var : Type} : Coe Var (Cslib.LambdaCalculus.LocallyNameless.Untyped.Term Var) := ⟨fvar⟩

This allows ⟪[fvar "abc"]⟫ₗ to be shortened to ⟪["abc"]⟫ₗ. I am now debating whether to reduce it further to ⟪"abc"⟫ₗ. While the Var type can be anything, String is the most common use case.

Should I make an exception for strings (and other common notations) to allow ⟪λ "abc" 3⟫ₗ instead of ⟪λ ["abc"] 3⟫ₗ? On second thought, keeping ⟪["abc"]⟫ₗ might be more consistent than creating special cases.

Another option is to attempt to interpret expressions as plain terms if they don't fit the lambda syntax, though this might complicate debugging.

Once this job is done, I have a plan to submit a PR. Is there anything else I should consider or might have missed?

This all seems reasonable. I actually had this before CSLib and it got lost in the initial port, so thanks for reviving it! Some specific thoughts:

  • the coercions seem fine
  • I don't understand the piece about []. In the blog they use ~ for antiquotes, this seems fine? I assumed using $ was problematic for whatever reason
  • special casing strings as free variables is fine by me
  • I'd consider the ergonomics of allow opening/closing/substitution within this syntax category
Thanks for responding my suggestions. I will change the antiquotation notation for [_] into ~ before submitting the PR.

About ergonomics, within this simple syntax category for the locally nameless lambda terms, there is no let in notations so I postponed to implement it. But I am trying to extend it to another lambda systems, so I probably face the work to implement it.

However, I think implementing the scope system in this post as it is had a little problem because we can use "meta-variables" with respect to lambda systems like ~x and ~y even for the binders and variables. For example, 

 fun (x : String) ↦ ⟪ λ ~(fvar x) ⟫ₗ

This will make it hard(probably impossible) to make an independent scope in this syntax.
I just meant deciding if/how you want to internalize the notations like e ⟦i ↝ s⟧, e [x := s], etc. into the syntax category.

Maybe doing it outside of this syntax category is not enough? I think
⟪ λ i ⟫ₗ⟦i ↝ s⟧ = ⟪ λ s ⟫ₗ
would work.
Yeah actually, I think it is probably fine to leave these outside the the syntax category. I don't think there are enough places where it would help readability to be worth duplicating.
